chunks: He said: Abul Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Jurjurai reported to me from Ishaq ibn Abdus, who reported from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Sulaiman al-Hadhrami, who reported from Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Ahmasi, who reported from al-Maharibi, from Ibn Abi Laila, from al-Hakam ibn Utaibah, from Ibn Abu al-Darda', from his father who said:

A man defamed another man in the presence of the Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, so a man from the people present refuted him. Then the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his progeny, said: "Whoever defends the honour of his brother, that act will be a shield for him from the Hellfire."

key_terms.حجابا من النار: Hijab min al-Nar: a shield or barrier from the Hellfire
key_terms.عرض: 'Ird: a person's honour, reputation, and dignity

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about defending someone's honour from slander?
ai.summary: Abu al-Darda' reports that a man slandered another in the Prophet's presence, and when someone from the gathering defended the slandered person, the Prophet (SAWW) declared that whoever defends his brother's honour, that act will serve as a shield from the Hellfire. This hadith, narrated in al-Amali of al-Mufid's 40th assembly, establishes defending others' reputations as both a social obligation and a means of earning divine protection.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 2. He said: Abu Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Jurjurai reported to me from Ishaq ibn Abdus, who reported from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Sulaiman al-Hadhrami, who reported from Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Ahmasi, who reported from Al-Maharibi, from Ibn Abi Laila, from al-Hakam ibn Utaibah from Ibn Abu al-Darda’, from his father who said:

A man defamed and slandered another man in presence of the Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, so a person from the people present, refuted him. The Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, said: "Whoever defends the honour of his brother, that act will shield him from hellfire."
